video_caption: The video opens with an abstract blue background of geometric shapes. Two white blocks, resembling elements from a periodic table, display the letters "T" with "1,987" above it, and "He" with "9,187" above it. Over the next few seconds, more similar blocks slide into place from the sides, forming the words "THE PERIODIC TABLE" using chemical symbols. Specifically, "Pe" (5,543), "Ri" (6,432), "O" (7,321), "Di" (8,210), "Ta" (2,876), "B" (3,765), "Le" (4,654), and "C" (9,100) appear. Above the word "PERIODIC", a blue triangular flag with the word "TRULY" (English) emerges and points to the words. As the words "THE PERIODIC TABLE" are fully formed, the blue background quickly transitions to black, and the element blocks scatter and shrink, fading into the distance. The "TRULY" flag remains, with a white line extending downwards from its base.

The video opens with numerous small, light blue spheres scattered on a white background, which then converge to form the number "118" in the same light blue color. The background swiftly changes to a vibrant blue, and the spheres vanish, leaving the number "118" in white text, below which "ELEMENTS" appears. A dark grey circular frame with a dashed outline then encircles the central text, featuring 16 rotating white icons representing various objects like a television, pizza slice, eyeglasses, headphones, an MP3 player, a camera, a DNA helix, a diamond, a barbell, a gamepad, a soccer ball, and medical pills. The frame and icons disappear, and the number "118" is replaced by "94" next to it, with the text below changing to "ELEMENTS NATURE." A grid of dashed white lines emerges as a background. Seven white icons representing natural elements—a ringed planet, an apple, a tree, a dog, the sun, a cloud, and a shark—appear on the screen. The scene transitions to a plain blue background where a white silhouette of a person stands. A small, unlit lightbulb icon falls from above onto the person's head, immediately replaced by a larger, lit lightbulb icon, signifying an idea. The person and lightbulb disappear, and the blue background splits, revealing a laboratory setting with a large beaker containing green liquid and a smaller flask with dark liquid, both bubbling. Inside the large beaker, the text "24 ELEMENTS LABORATORY" appears. The scene then shifts to a dark blue background depicting a stylized solar system with a large yellow sun and several smaller, colored planets orbiting along dotted white paths. The camera zooms in on the sun, where "94%" appears inside it. A white card displaying a periodic table entry for Hydrogen ("1 1,007 H Hydrogen") slides into view next to the sun, indicating its composition. The scene quickly changes back to a white background with a blue silhouette of a person. A white circular dial with yellow hour marks appears around the person on a blue background. The dial gradually fills with color segments, starting with a light blue segment that is labeled "65kg OXYGEN O" via a white rectangular tag, then a yellow segment labeled "18kg CARBON C", and finally a light grey segment labeled "10kg HYDROGEN H", illustrating the human body's elemental composition. The dial and person fade, and a dynamic pattern of light blue and dark blue geometric triangles forms against a white background. As each new triangle forms and connects, an essential element's name appears in white text: "NITROGEN," "CALCIUM," "PHOSPHORUS," "POTASSIUM," "SULPHUR," "SODIUM," "CHLORINE," "MAGNESIUM," "IRON," "COBALT," "COPPER," "ZINC," "IODINE," "FLUORINE," and "SELENIUM."

The video segment opens with a white background filled with numerous light blue circles, some containing chemical symbols (Hg, He, Cu, Ca, Fe, B, Au, H, S, Mg, O, Br, N, P, Zn, Ag, Pt, Na, Cl, C), representing different chemical elements. Yellow lines connect some of these circles, illustrating the formation of various chemical compounds like sodium chloride (Na-Cl) and a carbon-oxygen-silver chain (Ag-C-O-O). As the narration explains the "infinite number of possible combinations that produce all the different chemical compounds needed to keep us alive and build everything around us," the connections shift and new compounds are formed, for example, a copper-sulfur bond (S-Cu) and a zinc-oxygen chain (Zn-O-O). The scene then transitions to a white background where three blue circles, labeled "H", "O", and "H", appear. Yellow lines connect them to form a water molecule (H-O-H), and multiple such molecules then float around the screen, illustrating the water we drink. Following this, the screen turns entirely blue and fills with white bubbles, before a clear glass, outlined in black, appears and fills with this bubbly blue liquid. A dashed line highlights the rim of the glass, displaying the text "GLASS SiO2" (GLASS Silicon Dioxide). The blue background remains as a white, rotating 3D cube appears. A dashed circular outline on the cube is highlighted, with a line pointing to the text "SUGAR C12H22O11" (SUGAR Carbon 12 Hydrogen 22 Oxygen 11). Next, a white teacup and saucer appear, and a dark brown coffee bean-like object drops into the cup. A dashed circle around the bean highlights it, with the text "COFFEE C+H+N+O" (COFFEE Carbon+Hydrogen+Nitrogen+Oxygen). A silver spoon then drops into the cup, stirring the coffee. Two dashed lines emerge: one from the cup with the text "CUP Al+O+Si+H+Na+Ca" (CUP Aluminum+Oxygen+Silicon+Hydrogen+Sodium+Calcium), and another from the spoon with the text "SPOON Fe+C+Ni+Cr" (SPOON Iron+Carbon+Nickel+Chromium). This image then transitions to appear on the screen of a gray laptop. A dashed line highlights the laptop's plastic casing, revealing the text "PLASTIC C+H+Cl" (PLASTIC Carbon+Hydrogen+Chlorine). The scene shifts to a blue faceted globe, upon which a blue car is parked next to a gas pump, being refueled. The gas pump detaches, and the car drives off. The background then changes to a darker blue polygonal pattern, where two complex white 3D structures, identified as "PROTEINS," rotate within dashed circles. Below them, a white double helix structure, labeled "DNA," appears and rotates, emphasizing that "Everything around us and inside us are atoms that combined." Finally, the video transitions to a white background where blue dashed lines draw an abstract representation of an atom, starting with an orbital path, then developing into a spherical shape with multiple intersecting orbits. This abstract representation then fills with a red and green core and clarifies the blue lines as electron shells, with the text "CORE" (CORE) pointing to the nucleus, as the narration concludes, "An atom is the smallest recognizable constituent..."

The video segment opens with a detailed illustration of an atom's core, showing a cluster of red spheres labeled "PROTONS ⊕" (Protons) and a cluster of yellow spheres labeled "NEUTRONS" within a larger blue circle, which is itself labeled "CORE." This core is centrally located within a light blue, dashed spherical outline. At 0:06, the core shrinks into a tiny central point, and light blue dots representing electrons begin orbiting it in multiple dashed, elliptical paths within the spherical outline. This transitions at 0:09 to a representation of an atom as a central dark point surrounded by a large, soft blue gradient circle, with text appearing on the right: ""CLOUD" OF ELECTRONS ⊖" (Cloud of Electrons). The electron cloud then dissipates at 0:12, and the atom is again depicted with a small central nucleus and electrons orbiting in dashed circular paths, first with one electron layer, then two layers, showing distinct electron points moving along these paths. At 0:20, three such atoms are shown side-by-side, then more appear, arranging themselves around a central atom in a cross pattern, with their outermost dashed orbits overlapping slightly. At 0:27, a single atom is shown close-up, with its central nucleus and several inner dashed circular electron layers. A single electron is highlighted moving on the outermost layer, which then solidifies into a yellow band labeled "OUTER LAYER." Finally, from 0:37 to 0:43, multiple atoms of varying sizes, each with a central nucleus, gray inner electron layers (represented by multiple concentric circles with small dots), and a prominent yellow outer layer, are displayed on a white background. Initially scattered, some of these atoms then move to overlap and interact with each other.

The video segment begins on a light blue grid background, where individual element blocks from the periodic table, displaying the element's symbol, atomic number, atomic weight, and full name (e.g., Rf for Rutherfordium, Db for Dubnium, Sg for Seaborgium, Ta for Tantalum), appear and stack in a "Tetris-like" manner, gradually forming a large central section of the periodic table. More blocks drop into place, completing various rows and columns, until the entire periodic table, including the lanthanide and actinide series at the bottom, is fully assembled at 0:17, showing elements from Hydrogen (H) up to Oganesson (Uuo). The background then transitions to a white grid at 0:20, and the periodic table begins to reconstruct from scratch, with elements like Hydrogen (H), Helium (He), Lithium (Li), Beryllium (Be), and others appearing sequentially, filling out the table in a left-to-right, top-to-bottom order until the full periodic table is once again displayed. At 0:38, the table deconstructs, with columns of elements vanishing from right to left, followed by rows disappearing from bottom to top, before rapidly rebuilding with blocks of elements appearing back into a partial periodic table.

The video segment starts with a periodic table outline on a white background, where the first column (Group 1) elements are highlighted in blue: Hydrogen (H), Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), Cesium (Cs), and Francium (Fr). Alongside, their atomic models are displayed, each increasing in size from H to Fr, and consistently showing a single yellow electron in their outermost shell. The text labels for these elements include their symbol, atomic mass, and name, such as "H 1.007" for Hydrogen and "Fr 223.019" for Francium. The scene then transitions, clearing the previous elements and highlighting the last column (Group 18) elements: Helium (He), Neon (Ne), Argon (Ar), Krypton (Kr), Xenon (Xe), Radon (Rn), and Ununoctium (Uuo). Their atomic models appear, again growing in size, but in contrast, their outermost electron shells are completely filled with yellow electrons. Text labels like "He 4.002" for Helium and "Uuo 294.0" for Ununoctium are visible. The video then focuses on the element Potassium (K), represented by a blue square with "19 K Potassium 39.09" and its atomic model, which has one outermost electron. The periodic table outline reappears, highlighting the column above and below Potassium, showing Sodium (Na, "11 Na Sodium 22.989") and Rubidium (Rb, "37 Rb Rubidium 85.46"), respectively, with their atomic models also displaying a single outermost electron. Finally, Calcium (Ca), labeled "20 Ca Calcium 40.078", which is to the right of Potassium, is highlighted. Its atomic model is shown with an additional yellow electron in its outermost shell, marked "+1 ELECTRON", and an additional proton in its nucleus, marked "+1 PROTON".

The video segment opens with a partial view of the periodic table, featuring elements Hydrogen (H), Lithium (Li), Beryllium (Be), Sodium (Na), and Magnesium (Mg) outlined with dotted lines against a white background. Lithium (Li) is highlighted in a blue square with its atomic number "3" and atomic mass "6,941". A circular Bohr model of a Lithium atom, showing a grey nucleus and one black dot representing an electron in its outermost yellow ring, appears to the left. The animation then proceeds to Beryllium (Be), with a blue circle displaying "3 + 1" before highlighting Beryllium's square (atomic number "4", atomic mass "9,012"), and a corresponding Bohr model showing two outermost electrons. The focus shifts to elements Boron (B) through Neon (Ne), sequentially highlighting them in blue squares. For Boron, a blue circle with "4 + 1" appears, leading to Boron's square (atomic number "5", atomic mass "10,811"). The sequence continues to highlight Carbon (C), Nitrogen (N), Oxygen (O), Fluorine (F), and finally Neon (Ne) (atomic number "10", atomic mass "20,179"). A Bohr model of a Neon atom, depicting a full outermost electron shell, is shown. The scene then transitions back to the initial section of the periodic table, again highlighting Lithium (Li) and its Bohr model, then highlighting Sodium (Na) (atomic number "11", atomic mass "22,989") directly below Lithium. A Bohr model for Sodium appears below Lithium's, showing a more complex atomic structure but still with one electron in its outermost shell, illustrating the periodic recurrence of chemical properties. At 0:33, a loud, continuous buzzing sound begins. The periodic table and the atomic models quickly disappear, and the screen turns completely white. A grey circle emerges from the center of the screen, expanding to fill the frame before rapidly shrinking back to a small dot and vanishing, as the buzzing sound continues and then fades out.

The segment opens with a stylized atomic model featuring a grey core and concentric rings. Small white dots, representing electrons, sequentially fill the rings: two in the innermost ring, then eight in the second, and eighteen in the third, with the rings coloring in shades of blue and grey as they fill. At 0:18, this atomic model collapses into a thin vertical line, and the background shifts to an animated blue geometric pattern of triangles. White tiles, each displaying an element's symbol, name, atomic number, and atomic mass, begin to appear and arrange themselves to form the periodic table of elements. The assembly starts from the central transition metals and expands outwards, eventually showing the complete periodic table, including the lanthanides and actinides at the bottom, by 0:36. The periodic table then fades out, replaced by a scrolling white bar with text credits over the blue background. The text reads: "SCIENTIFIC CONSULTANCY PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) MOTION GRAPHICS / POST PRODUCTION RUI BRAZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) COORDINATION PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) AND MARIANA BARROSA (SCIENCE OFFICE) EXECUTIVE COORDINATION MARIANA BARROSA (SCIENCE OFFICE) ORIGINAL SCRIPT PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) SCIENTIFIC CONSULTANCY PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) MOTION GRAPHICS / POST PRODUCTION RUI BRAZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) DESIGN AND ILLUSTRATION ANTÓNIO CRUZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) MUSIC PAULO RAIMUNDO (SCIENCE OFFICE) NARRATION JAMES CLAMP" (SCIENTIFIC CONSULTANCY PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) MOTION GRAPHICS / POST PRODUCTION RUI BRAZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) COORDINATION PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) AND MARIANA BARROSA (SCIENCE OFFICE) EXECUTIVE COORDINATION MARIANA BARROSA (SCIENCE OFFICE) ORIGINAL SCRIPT PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) SCIENTIFIC CONSULTANCY PAULO RIBEIRO CLARO (UNIVERSITY OF AVEIRO) MOTION GRAPHICS / POST PRODUCTION RUI BRAZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) DESIGN AND ILLUSTRATION ANTÓNIO CRUZ (SCIENCE OFFICE) MUSIC PAULO RAIMUNDO (SCIENCE OFFICE) NARRATION JAMES CLAMP). The bar then reveals "PRODUCTION science office" (a logo with the text "science office" and a blue molecular graphic) and "FOR universidade de aveiro" (a logo with the text "universidade de aveiro" and a green open book graphic). Finally, the bar moves up to display "PROJECT FUNDED BY" followed by logos for "Ciência Viva," "AGÊNCIA NACIONAL PARA A CULTURA CIENTÍFICA E TECNOLÓGICA" (NATIONAL AGENCY FOR SCIENTIFIC AND TECHNOLOGICAL CULTURE), "COMPETE," "QREN QUADRO DE REFERÊNCIA ESTRATÉGICO NACIONAL" (NATIONAL STRATEGIC REFERENCE FRAMEWORK), and "UNIÃO EUROPEIA FUNDO EUROPEU DE DESENVOLVIMENTO REGIONAL" (EUROPEAN UNION EUROPEAN REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT FUND).
